place.source_title: Phoenix Manufacturing Company, Forest & Wisconsin Streets

brief: Foundry and machine-works complex begun in 1875 (enlarged 1907 and 1952, demolished after 1985): two rubble-stone buildings that housed the original foundry and machine shop, attached to a massive red-brick erecting shop with a raised clerestory monitor roof and stepped gable ends, rows of tall segmental-arched window openings (many bricked or boarded) and a big central freight door. A plain one-storey concrete-block addition, a smokestack and a wide empty gravel yard complete the site.

facade.notes: the Phoenix Manufacturing Co. (Eau Claire WI, 1875-1952), HAER: a tall brick machine shop with a stepped gable end (clerestory monitor), every window and opening boarded, a big central freight door; an asphalt yard in front, a concrete-block addition beside -- recorded before demolition

why.note: a foundry and machine shop: a tall central bay for the travelling crane, lower side aisles, a monitor for light and smoke
the old riverside works closed as industry moved to new parks on the edge of town
